title: Refactor: result-plumbing and ergonomic multi-tool orchestration API
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improves multi-tool call ergonomics: introduces explicit result plumbing API, clearer retry semantics for parallel calls, and migration guide for OpenAI-compatible call wrappers.
description:
Motivation: customers building orchestrations that call multiple tools in parallel reported inconsistent behaviour when tool payloads arrived out-of-order or when retries rewrote connector inputs. This PR refactors the public surface for multi-tool calls to make result delivery deterministic and opt-in ordering explicit, improves retry semantics for idempotent connectors, and preserves the OpenAI-compat layer by providing a thin adapter.

What this change does (high-level):
- Adds a first-class 'result_plumbing' API on the chat/response surface that lets callers pin how tool outputs are merged into model context (by-name, by-order, or explicit mapping).
- Introduces a ToolCallOptions struct (server and client-side) with fields: idempotency_key, max_retries, prefer_sequential_merge, and failure_policy (ignore/abort/fallback).
- Changes the default behaviour for parallel tool fanout: responses are collected and injected deterministically by tool name unless prefer_sequential_merge is set.
- Enhances retry semantics so connector retries are coordinated with the runtime backoff controller to avoid thundering-herd on downstream systems.
- Preserves OpenAI-compat: the openai_compat shim now maps legacy 'tools' array into the new mapping surface and emits deprecation logs when callers omit idempotency keys.
- Adds a migration guide (docs/migration/multi-tool-result-plumbing.md) and compatibility tests for both shimmed and native usage.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc + API sketch: docs/design/multi-tool-plumbing.md
- [x] Server runtime changes: deterministic collector and retry coordinator
- [x] Client SDK changes: TS and Python wrappers with tests
- [x] OpenAI-compat shim adapter and deprecation path
- [x] End-to-end tests against mock connectors
- [x] Performance sanity check (latency and memory) on perf-canary

Commits summary: 
- a1f3b2c: introduce result_plumbing API types and default mapping logic
- b22e9d0: implement deterministic collector and retry coordinator in runtime
- c7d4a55: update openai_compat shim to translate legacy calls and emit warnings
- d4f8a12: add migration guide and docs examples
- e8b1f0a: SDK: typescript client ergonomics and convenience helpers
- f3c0b66: unit/integration tests + mocks for connector retries

Files touched (high level):
- server/runtime/collector.go (deterministic collector, ~200 LOC)
- server/runtime/retry_coordinator.go (backoff coordination, ~120 LOC)
- server/api/types.proto (new ToolCallOptions and result_plumbing enums)
- openai_compat/shim.go (adapter mapping and deprecation logging)
- docs/migration/multi-tool-result-plumbing.md (migration steps and examples)
- sdk/ts/src/tool_client.ts (TS helpers and typed options)
- sdk/python/redwood/tool_client.py (Python wrapper and examples)
- tests/e2e/multi_tool_flow.test.ts (e2e scenario with mocked connectors)
- perf-canary/configs/multi_tool_scenarios.yaml (load profile used for sanity checks)

Testing and CI: 
All CI checks passed after fixups. Notable items during CI: e2e tests against the mock connector were flaky on the first run due to a race in the mock harness; fixed by adding a simple latch in tests. Perf-canary runs show a median latency increase of ~3ms for the standard path (deterministic collector overhead) and a p99 within SLOs.

Review conversation (summary):
- Miguel: asked for clarification on default merge semantics and suggested that name-based deterministic merge be the default to avoid surprises for users who migrate. Also requested an explicit migration warning in logs.
- Asha: implemented name-based default and added a WARN-level deprecation log in the shim.
- Dana: requested stronger guarantees around idempotency keys and object-level checksum to prevent silent overwrites. Asked for test coverage simulating connector replay.
- Asha: added idempotency key validation and an integration test that simulates repeated delivery; included a short doc section on best practices.
- Omar: flagged potential breaking change in third-party connectors that rely on positional merging; recommended feature flag gating for one release.
- Asha: added a runtime feature flag (multi_tool_positional_merge) defaulting to false; documented rollout steps in the design doc.

Migration notes for customers: 
- New clients should prefer the explicit result_plumbing options. Legacy OpenAI-style calls continue to work via the shim but will emit deprecation warnings if they do not provide idempotency_key. For migration, enable prefer_sequential_merge for workloads that depend on positional order, or set the feature flag temporarily for cluster-wide compatibility.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: additional latency and memory pressure for large parallel fanouts. Mitigation: collector uses streaming aggregation and soft memory limits; perf-canary profile included a stress test and recommended batching thresholds in Optimize suggestions.
- Risk: third-party connectors that are non-idempotent could see duplicate side effects if retries are not configured. Mitigation: default failure_policy set to 'abort' for connector failure and explicit docs for idempotency_key usage.

Release/rollback plan: 
- Rollout via canary in three stages: internal cluster -> dedicated customers opt-in -> global.
- If unexpected failures are observed, disable the feature flag to restore legacy positional behaviour immediately.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the public SDK ergonomics lightweight and pushes complexity into explicit ToolCallOptions so consumers can opt-in to richer behaviour without surprising defaults.
